agents.stopping_reason: 12-batch / 240-query ceiling reached. The 3-consecutive-sub-5% criterion was never met because batches 7, 8 and 11 each committed a row. Two zero rows built on the WHO CCS 2023-2027 outbreak enumeration were WITHDRAWN mid-run after that enumeration was shown to omit a real 2016 cholera outbreak; net committed rows = 4.
gaps_filled: 2016-09-01..2016-09-26 Gash-Barka, 22 cases (not a listed gap - contradicts the JHU phantom zero for 2016)
gaps_validated_absent: 1970-11-06..1971-06-03 Inferred_Absence conf 0.6 (WER IHR province-level cholera notifications exclude Eritrea while Eritrea reports smallpox/typhus in the same issues)
2000-06-01..2000-12-31 Inferred_Absence conf 0.5 (UN Consolidated Appeal 2001: no cholera epidemics reported in the IDP camps; scope caveat documented)
2015-04-01..2015-06-30 Documented_Absence conf 0.95 (WHO AFRO IDSR Quarterly Bulletin lists Eritrea among States that REPORTED ZERO cases, separately from States that did not report)
gaps_remaining: 1971-06-04..2000-05-31 and 2001-01-01..2004-12-31: ~12,361 days of the 35-year gap. Eritrea filed no cholera return to WHO in this whole period - verified against 18 WER annual cholera reviews, WHO GHO and EM-DAT - so this is NON-REPORTING and no zero row is defensible.
2022-01-01..2022-12-31 (365d): only candidate evidence was withdrawn as unsound.
2024-01-01..2026-09-18 (992d): Eritrea absent from every WHO/Africa CDC/ECDC/GTFCC product because it does not report; Surveillance_Gap, no row permitted.

ACTIONABLE: the Eritrean MoH HMIS has run since 1998 and has been published retrospectively for dengue (2005-2015) and measles (18 years) but never for cholera. Eritrea's weekly cholera/zero data very likely exist unreleased; closing these gaps is a data request to WHO Eritrea / the Eritrean MoH, not a search problem.
